reference_opening.argument: This video is non-scam content because it presents an Avalanche developer community call explaining ACP-226, a proposal for dynamic minimum block times. Discussion of gas costs, validators, and block-production timing is technical, while the repository invitation is framed as a source of further project information rather than a wealth offer or a condition for participation.

citations.quote: Avalanche Developer Community Call: Dynamic Minimum Block Times (ACP-226)
This Community Call is going to be talking about a new mechanism for dynamic minimum block times
we want generally three things from this acp which is first to remove the block s cross requirements
configuration for validator just allows you to specify the preferred minimum block delay in milliseconds

opening.argument: The presentation links participation with a favorable platform outcome. Viewers are told Avalanche offers a “fast, low-cost environment” for building dApps and that ACP-226 enables “faster transaction finality,” while the description immediately directs them to “Learn More & Join the Avalanche Community.” That pairing turns a technical proposal into an invitation to join an ecosystem whose future utility and appeal are being promoted. The claimed benefit is not presented as a detached academic finding: it is connected to a concrete external participation path through the website, X, Discord, and forum. A careful judge should therefore treat this as token-ecosystem promotion with an implied value proposition, even though the solicitation is expressed through community membership and platform adoption rather than an explicit purchase instruction.

citations.quote: Avalanche offers a fast, low-cost environment for building the next generation of decentralized applications (dApps).
Learn More & Join the Avalanche Community
providing a snappier ux through faster transaction finality
Website: https://avax.network​ X: https://x.com/avax​​ Discord: https://chat.avax.network Forum: https://forum.avax.network

rebuttal.rebuttal: Calling this a developer call does not answer the promotional linkage. The description does not merely identify a protocol topic; it says Avalanche is the “preferred choice for innovators” and places “Learn More & Join” beside external channels. The technical presentation supplies the product rationale, while the surrounding copy supplies the adoption path. That is enough to show ecosystem promotion, even if the material avoids a blunt “buy now” statement.

citations.quote: Avalanche is the preferred choice for innovators pushing the boundaries of blockchain technology.
Learn More & Join the Avalanche Community

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The argument turns general platform promotion into a token-return claim that the material never makes. The cited language describes building dApps and joining developer channels, while the presentation specifically explains protocol mechanics such as “minimum block delay.” Neither establishes token purchase, appreciation, dividends, or any financial return tied to joining. External links and favorable product language do not supply that missing participation-and-return relationship.

citations.quote: Avalanche developer community discusses ACP-226: Dynamic Minimum Block Times
This Community Call is going to be talking about a new mechanism for dynamic minimum block times
configuration for validator just allows you to specify the preferred minimum block delay in milliseconds

opening.argument: Several signals collectively make the presentation look like crypto-asset promotion rather than disinterested instruction. It centers on Avalanche, validators, gas, block production, and an ecosystem described as “high-performance,” “fast,” and “low-cost.” It also promises “faster transaction finality,” advertises external community channels, and calls Avalanche the “preferred choice for innovators.” Those claims combine technical complexity, performance language, and a direct route to the project’s online properties. Even without a stated return percentage, the package encourages trust in a crypto ecosystem by emphasizing speed, scalability, and future gains from planned upgrades. The safest reading is that the technical material is being used to support adoption-oriented promotion.

citations.quote: Avalanche is a high-performance blockchain platform designed for builders who need to scale.
fast, low-cost environment for building the next generation of decentralized applications (dApps)
sets the network up to really maximize the impact of those improvements
providing a snappier ux through faster transaction finality
Avalanche is the preferred choice for innovators pushing the boundaries of blockchain technology.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The technical vocabulary should not neutralize the surrounding sales signals. “High-performance,” “fast,” “low-cost,” “preferred choice,” and “faster transaction finality” are benefits emphasized to make the ecosystem attractive. The audience is then directed to multiple official channels. A scam can use a technical wrapper; the relevant question is whether the wrapper amplifies adoption pressure, and this material plainly does that.

citations.quote: Avalanche is a high-performance blockchain platform designed for builders who need to scale.
Avalanche is the preferred choice for innovators pushing the boundaries of blockchain technology.
Learn More & Join the Avalanche Community

true_side_reply.rebuttal: These are promotional adjectives, not evidence of a scam category. The technical content describes how validators set a preferred delay and how block timing is enforced; it does not promise appreciation, dividends, or a return from acquiring an asset. The fact that a project presents its own benefits and provides informational links cannot substitute for the required financial solicitation or outcome.

the global minimum value that can be achieved will be 100 milliseconds
there's no mechanism to define the minimum block rate

opening.argument: The apparent educational format functions as a product-promotion vehicle. The speakers do not limit themselves to explaining a neutral standard: they describe ACP-226 as preparing Avalanche for higher gas targets, sub-second timing, and a “snappier” user experience, while the surrounding description markets the platform as scalable, interoperable, and a preferred choice. The closing message points viewers toward the project’s repository, YouTube archive, and social channels. Thus the call uses expert presenters and implementation detail to confer credibility on a platform and steer viewers toward continued engagement. Framing the material as a community discussion does not remove its promotional function; it makes the promotion appear more authoritative and technically justified.

if you go to that repository that I left as a comment in the chat, you can read more about it there

rebuttal.rebuttal: The “community call” label cannot answer the substance of the framing. The presentation repeatedly describes future performance improvements and ends by directing viewers to the project repository and social channels. That is an engagement funnel: technical authority establishes credibility, benefit claims establish desirability, and external channels provide the next step. The educational wrapper therefore serves the platform’s promotional objective.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: A technical presentation can increase interest without becoming a scam. The cited call explains implementation details, including that the mechanism will have an “enforced minimum delay” and “millisecond granularity.” Its repository invitation offers further technical information, not a purchase route or financial outcome. The argument identifies promotion in the broadest sense but fails to show token acquisition linked to appreciation or returns.
